finance.summary:
Today's most important finance news includes a landmark ruling by the Supreme Court of India, which has urged a probe into reports of hospitals directing patients to specific pharmacies for their medications, leading to a steep 5% drop in the BSE Hospitals Index.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India has teamed up with the Reserve Bank of India to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market, with the launch of the India Market Access portal in September 2025.

Indian equity benchmarks have experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices, with the Nifty 50 index closing down by 95.75 points, reaching 22,620.45.

A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher just as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress has condemned the detention of tribal students who were heading to Mumbai to protest, seeking the resignation of the tribal development minister and the department's commissioner.

In other news, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process "corrupt", citing an Indian election that didn't happen. This appears to be a mix-up with Brazil, which held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday.

Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP, and Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, claiming that his ability to execute illegal orders makes him a liability for the country.

India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by $18.34 billion in a single week.
